## 方舟计划 · 本科全程学习历程总结（2025–2028）


### 一、大一上（2025年9–12月）

**核心任务：建立数学直觉基础**

| 类别 | 科目 | 教材/资源 | 配套课程 |
|------|------|----------|---------|
| 学校课程 | 高等数学I（A类） | — | — |
| 方舟计划 | **Strang《线性代数导论》** | Strang（已购） | MIT 18.06 |
| 方舟计划 | 普林斯顿微积分读本 | Banner | — |
| 方舟计划 | Axler《线性代数应该这样学》 | Axler（半放弃） | — |

**阶段状态**：建立微积分和线性代数的基本直觉，打下数学基础。Axler半途而废，但Strang已启动。


### 二、大一寒假（2026年1–2月）

**核心任务：开启离散数学和算法**

| 类别 | 科目 | 教材/资源 | 配套课程 |

| 方舟计划 | **CLRS + MIT 6.006（算法）** | CLRS（已购） | MIT 6.006 |

**阶段状态**：离散数学和算法正式启动。概率论读本作为背景阅读。


### 三、大一下（2026年2–6月）

**核心任务：系统底层和算法并行推进**

| 类别 | 科目 | 教材/资源 | 配套课程 |
|------|------|----------|---------|
| 方舟计划 | **MIT 6.042J —— 完成** | MIT Course Notes | MIT 6.042J |
| 方舟计划 | **CSAPP —— 完成** | CSAPP（已购） | CMU 15-213 |
| 方舟计划 | **Strang《线性代数导论》—— 完成** | Strang（已购） | MIT 18.06 |
| 方舟计划 | **18.065（数据学习线性代数）—— 启动** | Strang（已购） | MIT 18.065 |
| 方舟计划 | **CLRS + MIT 6.006 —— 启动** | CLRS（已购） | MIT 6.006 |

**阶段状态**：离散数学和CSAPP完成，线性代数导论完成，18.065和6.006启动。这是知识密度最高的一个学期。


### 四、大一暑假（2026年7–8月）

**核心任务：算法进阶和数学分析**

| 类别 | 科目 | 教材/资源 | 配套课程 |
|------|------|----------|---------|
| 方舟计划 | **6.006 —— 完成剩余** | CLRS | MIT 6.006 |
| 方舟计划 | **6.046（高级算法）—— 完成** | CLRS后续章节 | MIT 6.046 |
| 方舟计划 | **18.065 —— 推进到第4-5章** | Strang（已购） | MIT 18.065 |
| 方舟计划 | **100B（数学分析）—— 完成** | Rudin（已购） | MIT 18.100B |

**阶段状态**：6.006和6.046完成，18.065过半，100B完成。算法体系和数学分析的骨架建立完毕。


### 五、大二上（2026年9–12月）

**核心任务：概率论、网络、线代应用三支柱**

| 类别 | 科目 | 教材/资源 | 配套课程 | 说明 |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| 方舟计划 | **6.431（概率论）** | Bertsekas（已购） | MIT 6.431 | 周内主线 |
| 方舟计划 | **CS 144（计算机网络）** | Kurose（已购） | Stanford CS 144 | 周内主线 |
| 方舟计划 | **18.065 —— 完成全书** | Strang（已购） | MIT 18.065 | 周末，暑假已推进到第4-5章 |

**阶段状态**：概率论、计算机网络、数据学习线代全部完成。三支柱全部站稳。


### 六、大二寒假（2027年1–2月）

**核心任务：统计学习、操作系统、计算理论三线推进**

| 类别 | 科目 | 教材/资源 | 配套课程 | 寒假目标 |
|------|------|----------|---------|---------|
| 数学 | **ESL（统计学习基础）** | ESL | Stanford CS229 | 第4-5章（线性回归、分类、重采样方法） |
| 计算机 | **OSTEP（操作系统导论）** | OSTEP（免费PDF） | UTK COSC 361 | **完成全本**（虚拟化、并发、持久化） |
| 锦上添花 | **Sipser《计算理论导引》** | Sipser | MIT 6.045 | **完成全本**（自动机、正则语言、上下文无关文法） |

**阶段状态**：OSTEP全本完成，Sipser全本完成，ESL推进到第4-5章。寒假结束时，你已具备了操作系统和计算理论的完整基础。


### 七、大二下（2027年3–6月）

**核心任务：深度学习、操作系统工程、因果推断三线推进**

| 类别 | 科目 | 教材/资源 | 配套课程 | 目标 |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| 数学 | **MIT 6.S191（深度学习入门）** | 官网讲义+Lab+花书 | MIT 6.S191 | 完成全部6个单元+Lab |
| 计算机 | **MIT 6.S081/6.1810（操作系统工程）** | xv6教材+源码+QEMU | MIT 6.S081 | 完成前4-5个核心Lab |
| 锦上添花 | **Brady Neal《因果推理导论》** | causalcourse.com | Brady Neal课程 | 前5-6周内容（图模型、d-分离、干预、do-演算） |

**阶段状态**：深度学习直觉建立（6.S191），操作系统实现能力成型（6.S081），因果推断框架建立（Brady Neal）。三门课均具备完整课程结构和验证闭环。


### 八、大二暑假（2027年7–8月）

**核心任务：DeepSeek全量学习 + 国产算力配套**

暑假是“纵深攻坚”DeepSeek技术报告（58页），NVIDIA和Linux作为“配套武器”。

| 阶段 | 周次 | 核心任务 |
|------|------|---------|
| 预热 | 第1周 | 浏览DeepSeek-V4技术报告全文，标记陌生概念 |
| 架构 | 第2-3周 | 深度研读MoE、MLA、CSA/HCA |
| 系统 | 第4-5周 | DSpark推测解码、KV Cache管理、分布式训练 |
| 训练 | 第6-7周 | FP8、Muon优化器、mHC稳定训练 |
| 整合 | 第8周 | 通读全文，整理“方舟式”解读文档 |

**配套穿插**：
- 华为昇腾 + CANN生态（V4适配的国产算力硬件）
- NVIDIA/CUDA（对照理解设计动机）
- Linux内核（系统上下文，按需查阅）

**阶段状态**：完成DeepSeek-V4技术报告的深度阅读，建立从数学→算法→系统→LLM架构的完整连接链。理解DeepSeek如何在国产芯片上实现这些设计。


### 九、大三上（2027年9–12月）—— 考研前最后一学期

**核心任务：计算理论 + 分布式系统 + 机器学习理论**

这是考研前最后一段自由学习时间，三门课应同时实现理论闭环（6.840）、工程闭环（6.824）、ML理论补充（6.867）。

| 类别 | 课程 | 核心内容 | 与已有知识的衔接 |
|------|------|---------|-----------------|
| **理论（主线）** | **6.840/18.404J 计算理论** | 可计算性理论、P/NP、空间复杂度、概率计算、交互式证明 | 6.042J + Sipser全本（寒假已完成） |
| **系统（主线）** | **6.824 分布式系统** | 20篇里程碑论文 + 4个Lab（Raft、GFS等） | OSTEP + 6.S081 + CS144 |
| **理论延伸** | **6.867 机器学习** | 统计推断视角的ML（分类、回归、boosting、SVM、HMM） | 6.431 + 18.065 + 6.S191 |

**阶段状态**：完成计算理论的理论闭环（6.840），完成分布式系统的工程闭环（6.824），6.867作为ML理论的补充。至此，你已完成全部方舟计划的课程学习，准备进入考研备战。

# csapp-summary-methodology  (global/feedback, created 2026-06-30)
> CSAPP方舟复述方法论——设计问题驱动+跨课程连接+事实核查的课程总结标准
# CSAPP 方舟复述方法论

## 核心原则
1. **设计问题驱动**：每章不以「这章讲了什么」组织，而以「这章要回答的设计问题是什么」组织。标题用「不是…而是…」锚定核心问题。
2. **连接而非罗列**：每个章节末尾必须有 `【连接】` 标签，指向方舟体系中其他课程/论文的具体衔接点（不能写「与XX课有关」这种空话）。
3. **卡点真实化**：`[我的卡点]` 不能是占位符。必须包含：我当时卡在哪里 + 为什么卡住 + 后来怎么搞懂的——像边界标记 O(1) 推导、信号位向量 vs 队列、dup2 原子性那样。
4. **零空洞赞美**：删除「精妙」「经典」「极致」「极好」等形容词。用事实和逻辑体现价值。
5. **天才设计点控制在 5-7 个**：选取标准是「对全书的统摄力」——理解这个设计就能串联多个章节。

## 事实核查铁律
- Roofline OI 公式：OI ≈ 2/b_prec（常数），不是 d_model/(2·n_layers)
- x86 ISA 年限：1978→至今，近 50 年，是二进制向后兼容
- COW fork 首个生产实现：SVR2.4 (1984)，非 Mach/BSD
- 链接器行为：GNU ld 单遍 L→R；LLVM lld 预扫描符号表可反向提取；gold 保持单遍
- CSAPP malloc 边界标记：header/footer 均为 4 字节（WSIZE=4）
- 微码（microcode）是 ISA 兼容性的具体机制：x86 CISC → µop 翻译层
- Memory Mountain 数值：CSAPP 3e Core i7 Haswell 实测峰值 ~18,000 MB/s，谷底 ~1,300 MB/s（非 ~12,000/~500）
- Y86-64 指令：12 种操作码类型，含变体共二十余条（非精确的 "18 条"）
- 异常分类：原书 Figure 8.4 为 4 行表格，非 2×2 矩阵（2×2 是二次抽象）
- 进度图术语：§12.5.1 用 "unsafe region"（不安全区域），§12.5.3 用 "forbidden region"（禁止区域），二者不同
- 流水线吞吐率公式出自 §4.4.3（一般原则），非 §4.5.9（PIPE 性能分析）
- 所有数字和年代必须核实来源，不能凭记忆

## 输出标准
- 格式：Markdown，无页码
- 长度：15-20 页（~16K 字符）
- 结构：方舟生态位 → 12 章设计问题 → 5 个天才设计 → 待验证问题（P1-P4 优先级）→ Roofline 附录 → 自查清单
- 预留：每章末尾 `[我的卡点]` 供用户补充个人体验

# thread-model-tutorial  (project/project, created 2026-06-23)
> CSAPP线程模型对比教程——主仆vs对等vs预线程化——已生成MD+HTML+PDF三件套
# CSAPP 线程模型对比教程

已生成三份文件在项目目录下：

| 文件 | 用途 |
|:---|:---|
| `线程模型对比——主仆与对等.md` | 源 Markdown（含完整代码、表格、参考文献） |
| `线程模型对比——主仆与对等.html` | 浏览器打印到 PDF（带打印样式表） |
| `线程模型对比——主仆与对等.pdf` | 直接可用的 PDF（fpdf2 生成，~400KB） |

## 内容结构
- §0 问题定义：并发服务器的本质需求
- §1 主仆模型（代码 + 堆分配原理 + 时序图）
- §2 对等模型（代码 + 时序图）
- §3 内核视角：惊群问题 / LIFO不公平 / SO_REUSEPORT
- §4 合题：预线程化模型（CSAPP §12.5.4）
- §5 四维对比总表
- §6 选择决策树
- §7 从第一性原理再看一眼（主从/SMP/管道）
- §8 参考文献（含 kernel commit、LWN.net、Cloudflare Blog）

## 关键发现
- 对等模型"架构上"无单点瓶颈，但"实现上"共享listenfd导致LIFO不公平（Google实测3:1）
- SO_REUSEPORT (Linux 3.9) 解决了竞争问题
- 预线程化模型 = 主仆的职责清晰 + 对等的预创建线程 + 生产者-消费者缓冲区的背压控制

Title: Scoping the AI curriculum: key competencies for future AI practitioners
URL: https://doi.org/10.1007/s43681-026-01021-6
Published: 2026-02-25T00:00:00.000Z
Author: James Weichert, Hoda Eldardiry
Highlights:
The sustained interest in artificial intelligence (AI) as an area of postsecondary study is evident in growing enrollment figures and in expanded course offerings focusing on subjects like machine learning, natural language processing, and computer vision. Yet, for the most part, the contributions of these courses to the development of future AI practitioners is considered only in isolation. We find that a comprehensive framework to conceptualize the combined impact of these courses throughout a student's college education is lacking. Building on our previous research-particularly a study of computer science (CS) student attitudes and competencies related to AI and AI ethics-in this paper we begin to apply key findings towards the conceptualization of an AI curriculum. We argue that this curriculum must rest on three content pillars: technical foundations of AI systems, social implications of AI applications, and effective uses of AI tools. Such a holistic approach to AI education is necessary to underscore the centrality of policy considerations to the alignment of AI systems with normative objectives, and to reinforce an efficient and appropriate incorporation of AI into students' productivity workflows. In an effort to imagine how the AI curriculum can better prepare the future AI workforce, we emphasize three core AI-related competencies that are currently under-developed among CS students studying AI. Then, we map each competency onto one or more skills which we argue should be fostered throughout the AI curriculum. Finally, we propose examples of curricular interventions to address each of these skills and provide one example of an AI-focused undergraduate course sequence, illustrating opportunities to construct a cohesive AI curriculum across multiple separate computing courses. In taking this 'curriculum-level' perspective, we proffer that our synthesis of disparate strands of inquiry through this paper constitutes an important contribution to the literature regarding the teaching about and teaching with AI.

Title: Does Every Computer Scientist Need to Know Formal Methods?
URL: https://doi.org/10.1145/3670795
Published: 2024-06-10T00:00:00.000Z
Author: Manfred Broy, Achim D. Brucker, Alessandro Fantechi, Mario Gleirscher, Klaus Havelund, Markus A. Kuppe, et al.
Highlights:
We focus on the integration of Formal Methods as mandatory theme in any Computer Science University curriculum. In particular, when considering the ACM Curriculum for Computer Science, the inclusion of Formal Methods as a mandatory Knowledge Area needs arguing for why and how does every computer science graduate benefit from such knowledge. We do not agree with the sentence "While there is a belief that formal methods are important and they are growing in importance, we cannot state that every computer science graduate will need to use formal methods in their career." We argue that formal methods are and have to be an integral part of every computer science curriculum. Just as not all graduates will need to know how to work with databases either, it is still important for students to have a basic understanding of how data is stored and managed efficiently. The same way, students have to understand why and how methods work, what their formal background is, and how they are justified. No engineer should be ignorant of the foundations of their subject and the formal methods based on these. In this paper, we aim to highlight why every computer scientist needs to be familiar with formal methods. We argue that education in formal methods plays a key role by shaping students' programming mindset, fostering an appreciation for underlying principles, and encouraging the practice of thoughtful program design and justification, rather than simply writing programs without reflection and deeper understanding. Since integrating formal methods into the computer science curriculum is not a straightforward process, we explore the additional question: what are the trade-offs between one dedicated knowledge area of formal methods in a computer science curriculum versus having formal methods scattered across all knowledge areas? Solving problems while designing software and software-intensive systems demands an understanding of what is required, followed by a specification and formalizing a solution in a programming language. How to do this systematically and correctly on solid grounds is exactly the supported by Formal Methods.

For CS2023, given the increased role of artificial intelligence in undergraduate com puter science, the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI) also joined the effort. Together, the three profes sional bodies set up a steering committee of 17 members led by two co-chairs. The steering committee in turn recruited international disciplinary experts in diverse areas of computer science to form the CS2023 task force. The tasks undertaken by the CS2023 task force included: (1) The knowledge model of the curriculum, consisting of 17 knowledge areas was updated. The concept of core topics was streamlined. Suggestions were provided for packaging courses from knowledge areas and packaging curricula as aggregations of courses. (2) A competency framework was introduced to enable adopters to build a competency model of the curriculum, which in cludes a framework for systematically identifying tasks, a format for competency specification, and an algorithm to use the competency framework to build a customized com petency model. (3) Experts were invited to write articles on curricular practices including social issues, professional practices, pedagogical concerns, and programmatic considerations. The goal of the articles is to summarize the state of the art, inform educa tors, and attempt to advance computer science education practices. The work of the CS2023 task force was first introduced in a spe cial session at SIGCSE 2022 [5]. A progress report was provided in a special session at SIGCSE 2023 [6]. The final version of the report will be presented during the proposed special session. In addition, the process of adopting and adapting the curricular guidelines will be discussed.

Title: This course will focus on Reinforcement Learning (RL), a currently very active subfield of artificial intelligence, and it will discuss selectively a number of algorithmic topics couched on approximate Dynamic Programming (DP) methods: approximation in value and policy space, approximate policy iteration, rollout (a one-time form of policy iteration), model predictive control, adaptive control, multiagent methods, ap plications to challenging combinatorial optimization problems, implementations using simulation and neural network architectures, and engineering and artificial intelligence applications, such as the high-profile suc cesses of the AlphaZero and TD-Gammon programs, which play chess and backgammon, respectively. The course will center around a sequential decision architecture, called approximation in value space, which involves two algorithms that are designed largely independently of each other but operate in synergy. We call these the off-line training and the on-line play algorithms; the names are inspired by the context of games, such as AlphaZero and TD-Gammon. In the context of these games, the off-line training algorithm is the method used to teach the program how to evaluate positions and to generate good moves at any given position, while the on-line play algorithm is the method used to play in real time against human or computer opponents. A key fact is that the on-line play algorithm tends to improve substantially the performance predicted by the off-line play algorithm, and thus its proper implementation, through one-step or multistep minimization, rollout, and terminal cost approximation, is the critical part of the overall architectural design. For this reason, our course will place primary emphasis on the on-line algorithm implementation possibilities. Starting from the AlphaZero and TD-Gammon methodology, we will aim to show that approximation in value space applies very broadly to deterministic and stochastic optimal control problems, involving both discrete and continuous search spaces, as well as finite and infinite horizon. Moreover, we will show that our conceptual framework can be effectively integrated with other important methodologies such as model predictive and adaptive control, multiagent systems and decentralized control, discrete and Bayesian optimization, and heuristic algorithms for discrete optimization. The primary emphasis of the course is to encourage graduate research in reinforcement learning through directed reading and interactions with the instructor over zoom. Prerequisites are a full course on calculus, and a first course in probability. The course will leverage a series of videolectures, slides, and other material from previous ASU offerings of the course, which are posted at http://web.mit.edu/dimitrib/www/RLbook.html All class material (videolecture recordings, slides, class notes, etc) will be posted at this website on Fridays, as well as at ASU/Canvas. Textbooks (optional): (1) D. Bertsekas, “Reinforcement Learning and Optimal Control,” Athena Scientific, 2019. (2) D. Bertsekas, “Rollout, Policy Iteration, and Distributed Reinforcement Learning,” Athena Scientific, 2020. (3) D. Bertsekas, “Abstract Dynamic Programming,” 3rd Edition, Athena Scientific, 2022 (on-line). (4) D. Bertsekas, “Lessons from AlphaZero from Optimal, Model Predictive, and Adaptive Control,” Athena Scientific, 2022 (on-line). (5) D. Bertsekas, On-Line Class Notes. Supplementary material: (1) Sutton, R., and Barto, A., “Reinforcement Learning,” 2nd Edition, MIT Press, Cambridge, MA (on-line; a valuable resource that approaches the subject from the AI point of view). (2) Research papers and monographs, available on-line.

6.390 (or equivalent undergraduate class) discusses the “How” or “mechanics” of such approaches. In this class, we expect that you know the “How” for much of supervised learning and decision making. To start with, we will learn “Why” behind the “How”. We will utilize Probability as our formal language. We will discuss estimators and theoretical guarantees, and generalization: does a good model fit on historical data lead to ability to predict future? Finally, we will have 40% of the course discusses unsupervised learning / probabilistic modeling to understand the structure within the data.

### Decision Making
...
In data driven decision making (in presence of uncertainty), we need to learn the model of uncertainty, given observations. The goal is to make “optimal” decision with respect to a long-term objective. The decision vs information timescale are critically important. The following diagram summarizes the framework of decision making,
...
The two key timescales are state or environment dynamics, and information dynamics. Depending on the two timescales, there are methods / approaches including optimizing given model of uncertainty, Markov decision process, and reinforcement learning.
...
| State Dynamics | Information Dynamics |
| --- | --- |
| Optimizing Given Model of Uncertainty | No change (or extremely slow) | Lots of historical information |
| Markov Decision Process | High | Lots of historical information |
| Reinforcement Learning | High | Minimal information, learn as you go |
...
One fundamental challenge in reinforcement learning is explore vs exploit: we need to make decisions based on incomplete information about the world; in turn the decision we make affects future data we get to see. so should we stick to a decision that seems best for the moment, or sacrifice near-term gain to get more information for future long-term decision making.
...
Reinforcement learning has found success in various applications such as robotics, automated game player, ads placement. And notably, in the recent success of large-language-models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT.

I returned to MIT during IAP (January term) 2026 to teach a new iteration of Missing Semester, a class covering topics that are missing from the standard computer science curriculum, with my co-instructors Jon Gjengset and Jose Javier Gonzalez Ortiz. Over the years, the three of us helped teach several classes at MIT, and over and over again we saw that students have limited knowledge of tools available to them, as well as techniques and underlying ideas behind these tools. Computers were built to automate manual tasks, yet students often perform repetitive tasks by hand or fail to take full advantage of powerful tools such as version control and IDEs. Common examples include manually renaming a symbol across many source code files, or using a nuclear approach to fix a Git repository. At least at MIT, these topics are not taught as part of the university curriculum: students are never shown how to use these tools, or at least not how to use them efficiently, and thus waste time and effort on tasks that should be simple. The standard CS curriculum is missing critical topics about the computing ecosystem that could make students’ lives significantly easier both during school and after graduation (most jobs do not formally teach these topics either). To help mitigate this, the three of us developed a class, originally called Hacker Tools in 2019 and then renamed to Missing Semester in 2020. Over the past several years, we’ve seen the course translated into over a dozen languages, inspire similar courses at other universities, and be adopted by several companies as part of their standard onboarding materials. Based on feedback over the years from the internet, along with our updated perspective from working in industry for several years, we developed a new iteration of the course. The 2026 edition covers several new topics such as packaging/shipping code, code quality, agentic coding, and soft skills. Today, we’re releasing the course for free online. As always, we’d love to hear any feedback from the community to help us improve the course content!
...
Modern CS degrees are great, but they often leave out practical software tools and concepts you’ll use every day as a software engineer. In 2020, Anish Athalye, Jon Gjengset, and I taught The Missing Semester to help bridge that gap. We never would have anticipated its reach and impact over the past few years. This year we reunited at our alma mater, MIT, to teach an updated edition, and today we released all the materials and video lectures online!

# CCAI9003 Artificial Intelligence AI Safety: Catastrophe, Alignment, and Governance
...
Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are rapidly improving in capabilities. This rapid advancement poses a potentially catastrophic risk to humanity. This course is an interdisciplinary introduction to AI safety. Students will learn about (i) present and future capabilities of AI systems; (ii) the potentially catastrophic risk that AI systems pose to humanity; (iii) AI alignment, which seeks to give AI systems goals that reflect human values; (iv) AI governance, which seeks to design optimal regulations and institutions for controlling AI systems; and (v) foundational ethical and philosophical challenges in designing safe AI. Emphasizing an interdisciplinary approach, the course draws on perspectives from computer science, philosophy, political science, and complex systems theory. Through discussions, case studies, and policy briefs, students will critically analyse real-world scenarios where AI safety plays a pivotal role.
...
On completing the course, students will be able to:
...
1. Communicate effectively regarding core catastrophic risks surrounding AI systems.
2. Understand core questions related to AI alignment.
3. Explain key proposals in AI governance.
4. Demonstrate competence in concepts related to safety engineering and complex systems.

现在所有资料齐全，我来进行一次完整的审计分析。

---

# 方舟计划审计报告

你的计划在**系统底层（CSAPP→OSTEP→xv6→6.824）**和**数学基础（分析→线代→概率→优化）**两条主线上非常扎实，这正是当前AI从业者普遍缺失的部分。但我找到了 **7 个结构性漏洞** 和 **2 个调度风险**。

---

## 🔴 漏洞一：强化学习——最大的盲区

**严重程度：致命**

你的计划包含 DL（6.S191）、ML 理论（6.867）、因果推断（Brady Neal），但 **没有任何强化学习内容**。对于一个以 AGI 为目标的人来说，这是不可接受的：

| 为什么必须 | 具体事实 |
|-----------|---------|
| **RLHF 是后训练的核心** | ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini 都用 RLHF，DeepSeek-R1 用 RL 做推理能力涌现 |
| **AlphaZero 范式** | 搜索 + 学习是通往 AGI 的最成熟路径之一，这是 Bertsekas（你已购）的专长 |
| **推理模型** | o1/o3/DeepSeek-R1 的核心技术是 RL + test-time compute scaling，2025 最热方向 |
| **多步决策** | Agent 框架本质上是序列决策问题，RL 是理论框架 |

**建议**：插入 **Stanford CS234（强化学习导论）** 或 **MIT 6.7920**，配套 **Sutton & Barto 第二版**（免费在线）。最佳位置：**大二暑假或大三上**，与 6.867 并行（基础相通的）。

---

## 🔴 漏洞二：AI 安全/对齐——你要建 AGI 却不考虑控制

**严重程度：致命**

你计划用四年积累的所有技能 "开始构建 AGI 系统原型"，但整份计划中 **没有任何对齐、安全、治理的内容**。这不是伦理选修课，是工程问题：

- **RLHF 本身就是 alignment 技术**——不理解它就无法理解现代 LLM pipeline
- **Constitutional AI**（Claude 的核心）、**机械可解释性**、**可扩展监督** 是 AGI 路线图上的关键拼图
- **Alignment faking**（2024-2025 的突破性发现）证明了安全是实际工程约束，不是哲学讨论

**建议**：至少完成：
1. MIT AISF（AI Safety Fundamentals）8 周阅读小组
2. Dan Hendrycks《AI Safety, Ethics, and Society》教材
3. **作为方舟计划正式课程，在 大三 嵌入**

---

## 🔴 漏洞三：编程语言 / 编译器——空白象限

**严重程度：高**

你学了 CSAPP（汇编）、CLRS（算法）、6.824（分布式），但 **编程语言和编译器** 是整张能力矩阵的空白象限：

| 连接点 | 为什么重要 |
|--------|-----------|
| **CSAPP → 编译器** | 你理解了 ISA + 流水线 + 内存层次，编译器把这些抽象回高级语言 |

Walter Rudin: Principles of Analysis. Due to the idiotic copyright laws a new version costs a bundle. You should be able to pick up a second-hand copy for much less -- or there are `international editions' of unknown (to me) legality for even less. You can also probably find scanned copies, but I would guess that these are simply illegal. The book itself you might find hard reading since it is very much the opposite of a bloated calculus textbook. Don't worry if you need to spend several hours on a page! Apart from going through most of one-variable calculus rigorously, a primary aim of the course is to ensure that students can write clearly and concisely. In particular it is not enough to blunder across `the correct answer', it is just as important to understand why things are true. See the comments on final grades below. Beyond calculus of one variable -- functions, differentiability and (Riemann) integrability -- we will talk about metric spaces. These are a very important class of topological spaces -- so the notion of continuity is defined for maps between metric spaces -- which are important in many areas of mathematics. The course is intended as a gateway to other undergraduate and hence to graduate courses. After taking this course you can take for instance 101, 102, 103, 112, 701, 901.

好，数据到了。让我做一次 **定量负荷审计 + 节奏合规检查**。

---

# 修正版审计

先说结论：修正版在方向上完全正确，但 **三个学期的负荷仍然过大，且大二上的节奏不符合你的"一门数学+一门计算机+一门周末辅助"原则**。下面对每个阶段逐一拆解。

---

## 一、大一暑假：负荷量化

真实的 MIT 课时数据：

| 科目 | MIT/Stanford 标准工时 | 你的目标 | 估计工时 |
|------|----------------------|---------|---------|
| 6.006 收尾 | 已知已启动，收尾 | 2 周 | ~40h |
| **6.046** | 15-20h/周（一学期） | 核心部分，降低期望 | **50-80h** |
| **100B Rudin 前7章** | 12 学分 MIT = 12h/周课堂外，10 周 120h+ | 完成 | **100-140h** |
| 18.065 ch4-5 | Strang，比 18.06 轻 | 推进 | 20-30h |
| CS234 前6讲 | 每讲 1.5h 视频 | 2 周 | 15-20h |
| **总计** | | **8 周** | **225-310h** |

**数学验证**：暑假 8 周 = 56 天，每天学习 4-5.5 小时 = 224-308h。**卡在边界上，可行但零余量**——生一次病或有一天状态差就崩。

**建议**：18.065 不要放在暑假，**前移到你现在到暑假前的空档期**。你已经在做 CSAPP 收尾 + 6.042J 收尾，6.042J 完成后到暑假之间有至少 4-6 周，可以插空推进 18.065 前 5 章（Strang 风格轻松，每天 1 小时足矣）。这样暑假释放出 20-30h = 3-4 天余量，用来缓冲 100B 的意外卡点。

---

## 二、大二上：违反节奏原则

这是最大的结构性问题。

你的节奏原则是：**一门数学（周中）+ 一门计算机（周中）+ 一门辅助（周末）**。

大二上目前的方案：

| 科目 | 类别 | 位置 | 工作量 |
|------|------|------|--------|
| 6.431 概率论 | **数学** | ✅ 周中 | 12-15h/周 |
| CS144 网络 | **计算机** | ✅ 周中 | 12-15h/周 |
| **18.065 完成全书** | **数学（本来应是辅助）** | ❌ 周末？ | **10-12h/周** |
| 凸优化 Boyd | 阅读 | 周末 | 3-4h/周 |
| 信息论 Cover & Thomas | 阅读 | 周末 | 3-4h/周 |

**问题**：18.065 是 **一门完整的 MIT 12 学分课程**，不是"小辅助科目"。Weekend 总负荷 = 16-20h/周，相当于 **又多了一个周中主课**。

### 解决方案

18.065 的正确位置不是这里。我建议的解法是 **"分割 + 前移/后移"**：

1. **18.065 前 7 章** → **大一暑假前**（插空完成，你已有 Strang + 18.06 基础，Strang 自己的书写得轻松）
2. **18.065 剩余 3-5 章** → **大三上某空闲周**或 **考研后**阅读即可

这样大二上的 weekend 释放给：**Boyd 凸优化（每周 3-4h）+ Cover 信息论（每周 3-4h）**。两本并行阅读实际可行，因为凸优化和信息论在概率论（6.431）中共享数学基础——你学 6.431 的同一周读对应的凸优化/信息论章节，**内容互相强化**。

修正后大二上：

| 科目 | 类别 | 位置 | 工作量 |
|------|------|------|--------|
| 6.431 概率论 | 数学 | ✅ 周中 | 12-15h |
| CS144 网络 | 计算机 | ✅ 周中 | 12-15h |
| Boyd 凸优化 | 辅助阅读 | ✅ 周末 | 3-4h |
| Cover 信息论 | 辅助阅读 | ✅ 周末 | 3-4h |
| **合计** | | | **30-38h/周** ✅ 健康 |

---

## 三、大二寒假：两个全本 + 一个 partial = 过载

数据说话：

| 科目 | 估计工时 |
|------|---------|
| **OSTEP 全本**（~40 章 + 习题） | 60-80h |
| **Sipser 全本**（~400 页，10 章，密集证明） | 40-60h |
| ESL 4-5 章 | 12-18h |
| **总计** | **112-158h** |

寒假 6 周 = 42 天，每天 **2.7-3.8h**。看起来可行，但问题不是总工时——是 **两本都需要连续注意力**：

- OSTEP 需要你 **写代码做项目**（并发、信号量、文件系统），不是纯阅读
- Sipser 需要你 **做证明题**，不是翻翻书
- 两本都要求「找一整块时间沉浸」

**建议**：**Sipser 提前启动**。Sipser 前 4 章（自动机、正则语言、上下文无关文法）的数学基础是 6.042J——**你现在正在学 6.042J**。大一寒假之后的空档，每周读 1-2 节 Sipser 前 4 章，到寒假开始时 Sipser 已经过半。寒假时期 OSTEP 主攻，Sipser 收尾 + ESL 4-5。

---

## 四、大二下：编译器 + 6.S081 = 项目冲突

| 科目 | 类型 | 工作量 |
|------|------|--------|
| **6.S081 xv6 Lab** | **项目重课** | **20-30h/周（MIT 评价：本科最耗时的课之一）** |
| 6.S191 | 轻度 DL 入门 | 6-8h/周 |
| Brady Neal 因果推断 | 阅读 + 视频 | 6-8h/周 |
| **CS143 编译器前 5 周** | **Stanford 项目课，4 个 project** | **15-25h/周（full version）** |

**编译器你只能选 self-paced 版（5-10h/周）**，不能选 Stanford 正式课程版（15-25h/周 + 4 个递增 project）。同一学期做 xv6 Lab + 编译器 project 是两个项目黑洞。

**建议**：
- 选择 **Stanford CS143 的 self-paced/edX 版**（5-10h/周，无需 C++ 大项目）
- 或完全推迟到 **大二暑假** 作为 DeepSeek 研读之外的下午调剂

---

## 五、大三上：第三门课的定位

你的方案是"6.867 或 CS224n 择一"。关键问题是这两门都不是"周末辅助科目"：

| 课程 | 工作量 | 性质 |
|------|--------|------|
| **6.867（ML 理论）** | 12-15h/周 | 研究生级统计 ML，证明密集 |
| **CS224n（NLP）** | 12-15h/周 | Stanford 研究生级 NLP，项目重 |
| **AISF（安全/对齐）** | 2-4h/周 | 阅读 + 讨论，真正的周末课 |

**建议**：大三上周末放 **AISF（安全/对齐）**，6.867/CS224n 推迟到考研后知识空窗期（大三寒假或大四上）。这是最优解因为：

- 6.840（计算理论）+ 6.824（分布式系统）本身已经是重负荷组合
- 考研需要时间
- 6.867 的理论与 6.840 部分重叠但节奏不同，强行并行两个理论课容易两边吃灰

---

## 六、"提前学完"的时间窗口

你提到了"有可能提前学完一些学科"。我找到了 **5 个可以提前释放的时间窗口**：

| 当前科目 | 提前启动方法 | 释放出的时间 |
|----------|------------|------------|
| **18.065** | 现在开始每周 2h 插空推进（Strang 轻松+基础已够） | 暑假 20-30h |
| **Sipser 前 4 章** | 6.042J 完结后（第 10 周后）每周 3h 读自动机部分 | 寒假 25-30h |
| **CS234 RL 前 6 讲** | 可以放在暑假任意零碎时间（每晚看一讲） | 0（已计在暑假内） |
| **凸优化 Boyd** | 与 6.431 并行——同一周学概率分布 → 读凸集/凸函数 | 保持节奏 |
| **AISF 安全对齐** | 大三上之前寒假就可以完成 8 周中的前 4 周 | 大三上 8-10h |

最大的杠杆是 **18.065 前移**（释放暑假 20-30h）和 **Sipser 前移**（释放寒假 25-30h）。

---

## 📊 修正后的最终负荷表

| 学期 | 数学（周中） | 计算机（周中） | 辅助（周末） | 总负荷/周 | 健康度 |
|------|-----------|-------------|------------|----------|--------|
| 大一暑假 | 100B Rudin (主攻) | 6.006收尾+6.046核心 | CS234 RL前6讲 | 4-5.5h/天 | 🟡 边界 |
| 大二上 | **6.431** | **CS144** | Boyd+信息论 | 30-38h | ✅ |
| 大二寒假 | ESL 4-5 | OSTEP（主攻） | Sipser 收尾 | 2.7-3.8h/天 | 🟡 偏满 |
| 大二下 | 6.S191（DL） | **6.S081 xv6（主攻）** | Brady Neal + 编译器(self-paced) | 32-46h | 🔴 6.S081+编译器冲突 |
| 大二暑假 | — | DeepSeek（主攻）+ 编译器 | AISF 安全(并行) | 4-6h/天 | ✅ 可并行 |
| 大三上 | **6.840（理论）** | **6.824（分布式，主攻）** | AISF 延续 | 30-40h | ✅ 但 6.824 lab 可控是关键 |

---

## 最后：两项对你最有价值的调整

1. **最关键的改动**：**18.065 从大二上周末移除**，现在开始插空推进。这直接解决大二上的节奏违规 + 释放暑假余量。

2. **编译器选 self-paced 版**，不要选 Stanford 正式课程（4 project 递增）。self-paced 版（5-10h/周）可以放进大二下周末与 Brady Neal 共存，或将大二暑假的下午空档复用。

其余的修正你已经做对了——特别是放弃强行两门择一（6.867 vs CS224n），接受大三上第三门课应该是 **轻量的安全/对齐阅读组** 而不是一门重课。

## 结论：修正版审计的修改方向正确，但有两个改动需要重新校准

这份修正版审计的核心判断是对的：**原计划的负荷确实过载，需要优化时间分配。** 修正建议中的大部分改动（如将18.065前移、拆分大二上的周末负荷、减轻大三上第三门课的定位）完全合理，符合你的学习节奏原则。

但有两个地方，审计的修改方向与你的目标存在偏差：


### 一、编译器（CS143）：审计低估了它对你的意义

审计认为编译器是大二下的“项目冲突”，建议选self-paced版或推迟到暑假。

**偏差点**：你的目标是“以逻辑为基础的AGI”，编译器不是“可选的系统课”，而是**理解程序语义**的关键工具。AGI需要能理解代码、生成代码、优化代码，编译器的前端解析（语法分析、类型推断）是你“逻辑推理”能力的工程映射——它能让你真正理解“代码为什么会这样运行”。

**修正方案**：保留编译器作为大二下的目标，但确实不能选择full version。办法是选择**Stanford CS143的self-paced版**（edX平台，5-10h/周），或者**MIT 6.1100的课件自学**（不做完整项目，只做语法分析和类型检查的简化实现），在暑假完成一个可工作的迷你编译器。这样不会与6.S081冲突，但能完整保留编译器在你能力矩阵中的生态位。


### 二、AI安全/对齐：审计把它定位为“周末轻量阅读”，不够硬核

审计把AISF定位为大三上的“周末课”，每周2-4小时。

**偏差点**：AI安全/对齐在2025年已经成为AGI的工程组成部分，RLHF、Constitutional AI、可解释性都不是“伦理选修课”。作为AGI的构建者，你不需要成为安全研究员，但需要理解它如何在系统层面工作。

**修正方案**：将安全/对齐视为需要**正式学习、工程理解**的模块。真正的做法是：**大二暑假或大三上安排2-3周时间集中完成安全/对齐的核心部分**（比如MIT AISF的8周内容压缩到2-3周集中完成，加上Constitutional AI论文的阅读），而不是分散在周末的“阅读组”中。3周时间足够完成这个模块的系统学习。


## 二、其他审计建议

除了上述两处，其余审计建议均符合你的目标和构建原则：

- 18.065前移 → ✅ 完全正确
- 大二上周末释放给凸优化+信息论 → ✅ 完全正确
- Sipser前移 → ✅ 完全正确
- 大二下6.S191作为轻量辅助 → ✅ 完全正确
- 大三上第三门课降级为安全/对齐 → ✅ 正确，但按上述修正方式执行
- 大二暑假DeepSeek研读 → ✅ 保持核心地位不变


## 三、最终判断

## 14. 附录：方舟硬件采购红线

> 学习计划的执行依赖硬件，但硬件采购必须服从「构建第一」原则——**工具不超过必要阈值，绝不因焦虑而升级设备。**

### 核心约束

| 约束 | 值 | 原因 |
|------|----|------|
| 笔记本单价上限 | **≤ 1500 元** | 2026 年否决的电脑已证明上限在此 |
| 采购触发条件 | 现有设备无法运行计划中某课程的具体 Lab（如 xv6 QEMU、CS144 实验环境） | 不因"怕以后不够用"提前购买 |
| 批量采购红线 | **不得一次性购买超过 1 台个人计算设备** | 防止"买一台学习/买一台娱乐"的分心模式 |

### 允许的例外

- **外设**：键盘/鼠标/显示器，只要总价 ≤ 设备单价的 30%
- **学习资料**：书籍、ZIM 离线维基（已有一份在工具箱中）
- **国产算力调用**：若有免费/低成本的昇腾云资源可用，可以使用——这不属于个人设备采购

### 采购流程

```
发现设备瓶颈 → 确认计划中的确需要 → 搜索二手/廉价方案 → 24 小时冷静期 → 下单
```

不经此流程的采购视为计划外消费。

Other than Rudin's analysis text (the first one), I've read Robert Strichartz's "Way of Analysis". Strichartz gives you a lot of motivation and information for most of the concepts, while Rudin just gives you enough for you to do on your own. I favor Rudin's text much more, since I enjoyed the effort required to fill in the gaps and thereby making you "do" a lot during the reading. Additionally, Rudin has a style that I believe many enjoys, for most of his proofs are elegant and stylish. Strichartz will explain much more during, before, and after a proof, but sometimes I feel that his explanations becomes a bit too wordy and too cloudy over the main point. Take it this way: Would you rather try to find a dull sapphire in a messy hay sac, or find a beautiful diamond hiding in a small pile of needles? (one requires sheer effort for something "okay", while the other requires much more effort and care, but to obtain something rather nice.)
...

Great data. Let me now process what I've found:

**1. Real Analysis (100B): Rudin vs alternatives**
The consensus is clear:
- **Rudin**: Gold standard, concise, elegant proofs, but extremely terse. Requires mathematical maturity. "Read Rudin first, suffer through it, then read Tao" is a common recommendation.
- **Abbott "Understanding Analysis"**: Much more readable, intuitive, better for self-study and first exposure. Less terse, more motivation. Problems are more accessible. But: not as comprehensive as Rudin, official solutions are instructor-only.
- **Tao "Analysis I"**: Excellent as a second book or supplement. Builds from Peano axioms. Very pedagogical but verbose.

Since the user is doing MIT 18.100B (which uses Rudin as the textbook), they're locked into Rudin. But they could use Abbott as a supplement for understanding. The key insight: **Rudin + Abbott together** is a common combination - Ru din for rigor, Abbott for intuition when stuck.

**2. Probability: Bertsekas vs Blitzstein vs Wasserman**
- **Bertsekas & Tsitsiklis** (their book): MIT's own textbook for 6.431. Intuitive yet precise. Good balance of rigor and intuition. The user already bought it. Perfect for their needs.
- **Blitzstein & Hwang "Introduction to Probability"** (Harvard): More intuitive, very readable, great for self-study. Less mathematical depth than Bertsekas.
- **Wasserman "All of Statistics"**: Too condensed, more of a reference.

The user already has Bertsekas and it's the MIT standard. Stick with it.

**3. Compilers: CS143 vs 6.1100**
- **CS143** (Stanford, edX): Self-paced, 18 lectures, 4 assignments (lexer, parser, semantic analysis, code generation). Uses C++/Java, targets MIPS. Known issues: old VM/docker setup required. Content: traditional, well-structured.
- **6.1100** (MIT): Team-based project building a Decaf compiler. More project-heavy, SSA-based, targets x86. Not self-paced - it's a semester course with fixed deadlines.

For the user's self-paced situation, **CS143 edX** is the right choice. It's self-paced, covers the full pipeline, and can be split into frontend (大二下周末) and backend (大三上周末). The practical issue (old VM) can be solved with Docker.

Highlights:
It has been well over five years since LWN reviewed the second edition of Robert Love's Linux Kernel Development. Needless to say, things have changed a little since the 2.6.10 release covered by that edition. As it happens, the third edition has been out for a few months now; your editor has finally had a chance to read through his copy and put together a review. In summary, the third edition is a much-needed update, and Linux Kernel Development remains a valuable resource, but there are some disappointments to be found as well.
...
All told, the coverage of the core kernel is well written and clear, in an approachable style. Linux Kernel Development is, at this time, probably the best reference available for developers wanting to learn how the kernel works and how the major pieces fit together. Your editor is glad to have a copy on hand.
...
And many things which should be discussed in a contemporary book aren't. Developers working on the kernel now should probably be familiar with control groups, contemporary debugging tools (kmemleak, lockdep, the fault injection framework, ...), debugfs, ftrace, git, high-resolution timers, huge pages, linux-next, multiple slab allocators, namespaces, perf, power management and quality of service, read-copy-update, readahead, reverse mapping in the VM subsystem, scheduler domains, splice(), TASK_KILLABLE, threaded interrupt handlers, virtualization, and so on. No book on the kernel can hope to be complete and still be something that a person of ordinary strength can physically lift, but these topics are all important enough that, one would assume, at least some of them would merit coverage, but none are mentioned in the third edition.
...
These grumbles notwithstanding, your editor will restate what was said above: this book remains the best overview of contemporary kernel development available today. Robert is a talented and engaging writer who is able to cover complex topics in a readily understandable manner. The third edition merits a place on the "L1 bookshelf" (the one which can be reached without getting out of the chair); developers who are working with the kernel will probably want a copy.

Highlights:
Where does a newbie start their journey into the Linux kernel? Device drivers is the most common answer. Despite its age, Linux Device Drivers 3rd Edition(LDD3) remains one of the best options for learning about device drivers. There are challenges in using such an old text. LDD3’s code examples target the`2.6.10` kernel. At the time of this writing, the kernel is at version`5.19`! That said, fixing API deltas just adds to the fun. This article talks about setting up an environment for LDD3 experimentation and the LDD3 experience itself.
...
For LDD3 development, option #3 is the best choice. This project adds the twist of containerizing the toolchain using Docker. Containerization has the added advantage of allowing you to reliably replicate and share your build environment.
...
LDD3 is a pleasant read given the subject matter. You’ll get the most out of this book if you come in with a solid grasp of the C programming language. Moderate knowledge of Linux development and good operating systems fundamentals are critical.
...
A strong selling point of this book is that you don’t need actual hardware to follow along. Throughout the book, you develop different types of Simple Character Utility for Loading Localities (`scull`) device drivers. The`scull` drivers manage an in memory device which removes the need for any specific hardware. Each`scull` version illustrates a new driver programming concept.
...
One of the fun parts of working through LDD3 was resolving issues in the example code. The examples run without modification on the`2.6.10` kernel. This project targets a more recent kernel release:`5.19`. The choice of using a more modern kernel breaks a few of the drivers. This forces you to navigate the kernel source code and the LWN archives in search of answers which often times leads to interesting threads regarding kernel design decisions.
...
LDD3 still holds up in 2022. Sure the example code needs some tweaking and a couple of the later chapters may be a bit dated. That said, the core concepts of the book remain relevant. Containerizing the kernel toolchain is a fun task. Not having to buy any specialty hardware to follow along with the examples in the text is a big bonus. Highly recommend LDD3 in 2022!

好问题。做完了全部横向对比，给你结论。

---

## 一、课程总量确实变了

你注意到的不只是错觉。这是增量明细：

| 来源 | 新增模块 | 原计划 | 现计划 |
|------|---------|--------|--------|
| 审计补漏洞 | **凸优化（Boyd）** | 仅"前瞻了解" | ✅ 正式阅读 |
| 审计补漏洞 | **信息论（Cover & Thomas）** | 缺失 | ✅ 正式阅读 |
| 审计补漏洞 | **编译器/PL（CS143）** | 缺失 | ✅ 完整课程 |
| 审计补漏洞 | **强化学习（CS234）** | 缺失 | ✅ 6讲视频 |
| 审计补漏洞 | **AI安全/对齐（AISF）** | 缺失 | ✅ 2周集中 |
| 审计补漏洞 | **NLP深度（CS224n）** | 缺失 | ✅ 视频自读 |
| 你的追加 | **CUDA导论** | 缺失 | ✅ 完整1周+动手 |
| 你的追加 | **昇腾+CANN** | 仅穿插一句 | ✅ 完整1周+动手 |
| 你的追加 | **Linux内核** | 缺失 | ✅ 完整2周+动手 |
| **总计** | **+9模块** | **~20模块** | **~29模块** |

但其中 **5 个是轻量级**（Boyd 前5章、Cover 前6章、CS234 6讲视频、CS224n 视频、AISF 2周），**4 个是完整课程**（CS143、CUDA、昇腾、Linux）。实际负荷增幅约 30%，主要集中在**大二暑假**那个集中期。

---

## 二、各科目教材/课程横向对比

### 1. 数学分析（100B）

| 候选 | 风格 | 适合自学的程度 | 结论 |
|------|------|:------------:|------|
| **Rudin**（你已锁定） | 极简、优美、证明密集 | ⚠️ 极难，MIT 标准教材 | ✅ **主线教材** |
| Abbott《Understanding Analysis》 | 直观、有动机、可读性强 | ✅ 公认最适合自学入门 | ✅ **辅助教材**（卡住时查阅） |
| Tao《Analysis I》 | 从 Peano 公理建起，极其细致 | ✅ 优秀但过长 | ⚪ 第二遍阅读 |

**推荐**：**Rudin 主线 + Abbott 辅助**。Rudin 是 MIT 18.100B 的指定教材不能换，但 Abbott 是你卡在第 4-5 章时的救生索。这是自学者最常用的组合。

### 2. 概率论（6.431）

| 候选 | 风格 | 结论 |
|------|------|------|
| **Bertsekas & Tsitsiklis**（你已购） | MIT 标准，精确而直观 | ✅ **无需换** |
| Blitzstein & Hwang（Harvard） | 更生动，偏应用 | ⚪ 可作参考但已购 Bertsekas |
| Wasserman《All of Statistics》 | 压缩过紧，偏参考书 | ❌ |

**推荐**：**保留 Bertsekas**。已购 + MIT 标准 + 与 6.431 直接匹配。

### 3. 编译器（CS143）

| 候选 | 形式 | 工作量 | 自学期权 |
|------|------|--------|:--------:|
| **Stanford CS143 edX** | 自定进度，18 讲，4 个 assignment | 5-10h/周 | ✅ **最佳选择** |
| MIT 6.1100 | 团队项目，有截止日期，SSA 后端 | 20h+/周 | ❌ 非自定进度 |
| nand2tetris 第二部分 | 从 VM 到编译器，极简 | 轻量 | ⚪ 太简单达不到你的需求 |

**推荐**：**CS143 edX**。注意：使用 Docker 而非官方 VM（VM 太旧）。edX 版可以让你在 大二下做前端 + 大三上做后端。

### 4. NLP（CS224n vs CS224u）

| 候选 | 覆盖范围 | 适合你的理由 |
|------|---------|-------------|
| **CS224n** NLP with DL | 词向量→RNN→Transformer→LLM→Agent | 你需要的 **Transformer/预训练/LLM 架构** 全在这里 |
| CS224u NLU | 需要 CS224n 做前置；NLU 专项（关系抽取/语义解析） | 太窄，你的 LLM 目标不适合 |

**推荐**：**CS224n**。你只需要看视频建立直觉（2 周 2x 速刷），不做作业。CS224n 的视频质量极高，且 2024 版已大幅更新 LLM 内容。

### 5. CUDA 学习资源

| 资源 | 形式 | 你的用法 |
|------|------|---------|
| **NVIDIA CUDA Programming Guide ch1-6** | 官方文档 | ✅ **主线教材** |
| **《Programming Massively Parallel Processors》Kirk & Hwu 第5版** | 教材 | ✅ **动手代码来源**（含 LLM 章节） |
| NVIDIA CUDA C++ Tutorial（GitHub） | Jupyter Notebook | ✅ 第一天跑起来 |
| freeCodeCamp CUDA 课程（YouTube） | 视频 | ⚪ 可选，背景补充 |

**推荐**：官方 Guide + Kirk & Hwu 教材 + NVIDIA 官方 Notebooks。三者互补。

### 6. Linux 内核学习资源

| 资源 | 风格 | 适合你的方式 |
|------|------|-------------|
| **LDD3（Linux Device Drivers, 3rd ed）** | 边做边学，动手写模块 | ✅ **主线教材**（旧但概念不变） |
| **Linux Kernel Module Programming Guide（更新版）** | 免费在线，适配 5.x/6.x 内核 | ✅ 解决 LDD3 版本过旧问题 |
| Linux Kernel Development（Robert Love） | 概览式，少动手 | ⚪ 辅助阅读 |
| Linux 内核实验室（linux-kernel-labs.github.io） | 动手实验 | ✅ **动手任务来源** |

**推荐**：**LKMPG（在线更新版）做动手主线**，LDD3 做概念阅读，Linux 内核实验室做 4 个动手任务。

---

## 三、总量控制建议

如果 29 个模块让你觉得多了，这里是 **可以砍的优先级**：

| 砍刀顺序 | 模块 | 理由 | 节约 |
